name: Unit Testing Best Practices
description: This module captures the best practices for unit testing, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.
content:
This module captures the best practices for unit testing, distilled from common failure modes and what tends to hold up over time.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Validate unit testing outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
2. Surface known limitations of a chosen unit testing approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
3. When multiple unit testing strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
4. State assumptions about unit testing explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
5. Before starting unit testing work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
6. Document any non-obvious unit testing decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
7. Prefer explicit, readable unit testing solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
8. Re-check edge cases relevant to unit testing (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
9. Keep unit testing changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
10. Keep unit testing outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
11. Measure before optimizing any unit testing bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid mixing unrelated unit testing concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not silently drop unit testing edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid introducing new unit testing abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for unit testing, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
